messages:
Anya: Quick sync — need a decision: bundle the VPC gateway connector in the private distro or ship it as a standalone edge-operator? Thinking about upgrade surface, customer ops burden, and handshake/fallback behavior. :thinking:
Jay: My leaning: ship as an operator. Independent upgrades, smaller distro. But it does add a controller customers must allow in their cluster. Upgrade complexity moves to operator lifecycle (CRDs, controller manager).
Hannah: Operator is nice for us, but heads up — several enterprise netops said they forbid any controllers from outside the core infra. They prefer a single distro artifact they can scan and run offline.
Omar: Performance note: bundled connector can live in the same pod network namespace -> fewer hops. Operator implies sidecar or separate pod which might add ~2-6ms p95 depending on topology. Not huge, but matters for low-latency SLAs.
Tina: From CS: splits in the field. Regulated customers (banking, pharma) want a single signed bundle for airgap installs. Startups and cloud-native customers prefer operator for faster patches. We should map per-customer preference.
Anya: OK — tradeoffs acknowledged. We need concrete rollout and fallback requirements. If we go operator-first, what's the safe fallback when handshake fails (e.g., connector can't talk to customer-managed router)?
Jay: Fallback matrix proposal (high level):
- connector healthy -> direct VPC peering / mirroring
- connector degraded -> local proxy mode (limited features)
- connector down -> route to Redwood-hosted relay (only for customers who opt-in)
This needs opt-in for hosted relay (privacy/legal).
Omar: Agreed. Also add a KV-cache grace mode: maintain last-known auth tokens & cached prefixes to reduce outages during flapping.
Hannah: Implementation constraint: operator path requires a new custom resource 'GatewayHandshake' with fields: desiredMode, relayOptIn, canaryTags. Many customers will need docs on required firewall rules.
Anya: Can we sketch a minimal rollout policy for operator to minimize blast radius? Something like canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with auto-rollback on error rate > 3% over 10m.
Omar: Yeah, something like below (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
rollout_policy:
  steps:
    - pct: 5
      wait: 30m
    - pct: 25
      wait: 2h
    - pct: 100
  rollback_on:
    error_rate_pct: 3
    window: 10m
```
Hannah: Need to add network validation preflight check: ensure CR can reach IP ranges and required ports. If preflight fails, operator should stay in "observe-only" mode and surface remediation steps.
Tina: Also add a customer opt-in checklist for hosted-relay fallback: legal sign-off, SLA exceptions, and data residency toggle.
deploy-bot: Created ISSUE-1428: "gateway-handshake-fallback-policy + operator vs bundle decision" and linked to spec doc https://internal.redwood/infra/handshake-proposal (assigned to @jay).
Anya: Proposal for next steps (action items):
- Jay: draft operator CRD + preflight checklist (due EOW)
- Hannah: doc firewall rules + airgap bundle notes for regulated customers (due next Wed)
- Omar: run perf microbench comparing bundled vs sidecar scenarios (p95 delta) and add to launch criteria (3 days)
- Tina: compile customer preference matrix and legal checklist for hosted-relay opt-in (next Thu)
Launch criteria (candidate list):
- preflight checks pass for >=3 target enterprise testbeds
- canary rollout instrumentation + auto-rollback implemented
- signed legal opt-in for hosted relay (if enabled)
- perf delta within agreed SLA (p95 impact < 10ms)
Anya: If no strong objections by EOD tomorrow I'll lock decision to operator-first with a documented airgap/bundle fallback path. :shipit:
Jay: Fine with operator-first as long as we commit to an airgap bundle (manual release) for regulated customers.
Hannah: Agreed. We'll add clear docs and an airgap build pipeline.
Tina: Sounds good. Will surface to the top 5 accounts to confirm.
Omar: I'll start perf runs and post results here.
Anya: Thanks team — syncing into roadmap now.
